candidate_decisions.reason: This item correctly warns that non-dominant smm, wsm, rbw, ayn and hdd projections do not establish lexical glosses. Retain that warning in friction. Reject it as a standalone wider reading: it supplies no particular carrier/trigger relation or changed reading; the five mappings are provenance, not five activated claims. No missing branch gloss is fabricated.

Preserve all three qualifications in friction: cultivated effects need not certify a name-mark, mercy/account need not stand in a one-way governing relation, and worship/yielding need not cause aid. As an uncertainty inventory this has no independent activated finding, and cannot establish those causal arrows merely by mentioning them.

Preserve the alternative that the mercy pair supplies emphasis without a generative-then-sustaining phase division. The record has no wider trigger proving either temporal phase or a staged reader change, so it is not a standalone global finding; the local root repetition remains visible in the surface evidence.

The coexistence of accountable, enclosing, navigational and transformative models is a containment policy, not evidence that all four activate. Preserve non-ranking in friction and qualify each actual contact separately. The record provides no specific wider trigger for a standalone finding.

Retain operative designation with a bounded relation to observable merciful conduct. Exclude the requirement that merciful provenance must be certified by cultivated, praiseworthy effects: no such necessity or cultivation-to-name proof is supplied, and this reconstructed summary is not an actual staged observation.

Retain accountable mercy and the worship/aid relation independently grounded by 39:11, 17:110 and 21:112. Exclude the asserted temporal or causal exchange 'yielded to, then enabled by' and any claim of a measured later revision.

Retain persistence and discrimination as continuing remembrance with a named-use boundary. Exclude the claimed guidance-road-straightness-benefaction-exclusion chain and literal name-mark: the unanchored summary supplies neither a road occurrence nor a physical mark/wayfinding operation returning to 1:1.

The inventory combines raised naming, visible marking, rain-marked germination, narrow entry, intended direction, private reconciliation, womb and kinship without binding them to particular triggers or changed readings. Review each available branch against actual wider evidence, but reject this summary as proof that the whole inventory activated. In particular the packet does not establish physical branding, first-season rain, or a narrow aperture for the opening. The evidential/ecological/juridical/agential/spatial/material/social taxonomy cannot itself create findings.

findings.title: An act performed under the merciful name
findings.claim: The opening names the merciful Allah as the one under whose name an act is undertaken; the same wording can accompany an authored message and an undertaking with movement and rest.
findings.mechanism: In 27:30 the full formula is attached to what is from Sulayman; 11:41 attaches naming Allah to the vessel's course and mooring and explicitly names mercy. These distinct acts give the compressed governing act of bi-smi an operative range.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening can orient the act now being performed, with mercy characterizing its named referent.
findings.containment: The formulation remains an invocation. It neither grants every speaker divine authorization nor promises success; the projected sequence of all later Fatiha acts is excluded.

epistemic.reason: The legacy nomination is retained only to the extent independently grounded by the supplied wider Arabic and exact branch facets; its reconstruction is not a staged observation.

findings.title: Mercy alongside reckoning
findings.claim: The mercy named at the opening remains compatible with sovereign judgment and accountability; it can precede an encounter with that authority without cancelling it.
findings.mechanism: 6:12 joins Allah's ownership, mercy prescribed upon himself, and gathering to resurrection. 19:45 explicitly warns of punishment from al-Rahman, while 78:38 makes speech depend on al-Rahman's permission. findings.containment: Mercy does not lose its ordinary beneficent sense. These texts do not resolve the distribution of punishment or forgiveness, and do not establish a literal enclosure around a tribunal.

findings.mechanism: 7:180 links names to the act of calling through them; 17:110 names Allah and al-Rahman as invocations of the same referent. These acts meet the opening preposition's attachment to ism.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening's reference becomes an act of directed address rather than reference without a speaker's orientation.
findings.containment: No compulsory elided verb is assigned. The name's ordinary identifying role is preserved, and the focus has no explicit exclusive particle.

epistemic.reason: The legacy nomination is retained only to the extent independently grounded by the supplied wider Arabic and exact branch facets; its reconstruction is not a staged observation.

findings.title: Raising mention through honor
findings.claim: The name can carry a qualified elevation image when its utterance meets explicit honor directed to the named one.
findings.mechanism: 55:78 blesses the Lord's name. This independent act of honor meets the source etymology that naming raises mention, allowing upward movement to be heard analogically through ism while the word continues to mean name.
findings.reader_payoff: Naming can be an honoring act with a discernible direction in the speaker's attention.
findings.containment: The elevation concerns mention in speech, not an increase in Allah's worth. Good repute spreading through a population and the local sequence of praise and repetition are not established.

findings.title: Formative protection
findings.claim: Mercy can be imagined as protecting a dependent through development, through the mercy root's womb image and the explicitly depicted developmental sequence in 22:5.
findings.mechanism: 22:5 gives retention in wombs, a determined term, childhood, and growth. Those ordered events activate the registered womb-as-developmental-container facet associated with the mercy epithets.
findings.reader_payoff: The epithets can suggest care lasting through development rather than a momentary response.
findings.containment: The sequence belongs to created human life. It does not assign generation to al-Rahman and maintenance exclusively to al-Rahim, or establish womb as either epithet's literal meaning.

epistemic.reason: The legacy nomination is retained only to the extent independently grounded by the supplied wider Arabic and exact branch facets; its reconstruction is not a staged observation.

findings.title: Directed appeal and protected dependence
findings.claim: The opening can hold both a definite addressee for invocation and a bounded image of care enabling dependent life; these are distinct relations, not a compulsory single transformation.
findings.mechanism: 17:110 connects invocation of Allah and al-Rahman, returning to the name's referent; 22:5 independently supplies the gestational-developmental carrier for the mercy root's womb image. The two contacts make relational address and developmental dependence available together.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can retain the named addressee while also picturing the vulnerable life to which mercy reaches.
findings.containment: This is a reconstruction from independently supplied wider evidence. It does not claim an observed before/after correction from the missing 1:5 and 1:2-1:6 surfaces, or causal proof that mercy creates every act of guidance.

findings.title: The invoked mercy has a conduct-facing resonance
findings.claim: The merciful name invoked at the opening can orient peaceful and reparative conduct, and that conduct can provide a qualified sign of the orientation.
findings.mechanism: 25:63 identifies servants of al-Rahman by their manner of walking and peaceful response; 2:182 joins reconciliation between people with Allah's forgiving mercy. Their concrete conduct returns through the mercy epithets. Under the packet's explicitly supplied non-dominant wsm mapping, the visible-conduct description in 25:63 also activates sign-based inference through ism: a named orientation can become legible in effects.
findings.reader_payoff: An invocation can have an ethical direction with visible human effects.
findings.containment: These are examples of conduct associated with mercy, not a test that proves the divine provenance of an act or a requirement to infer every person's inner state. No cultivated vegetation or mandatory public certification is inferred. The sign-reading analogy does not authorize physiognomic judgments or establish an inner quality with certainty.

epistemic.reason: The legacy nomination is retained only to the extent independently grounded by the supplied wider Arabic and exact branch facets; its reconstruction is not a staged observation. Its sign-reading component uses the packet's non-dominant wsm projection as an analogy, without asserting that projection as the surface word's lexical root.

findings.title: Devotion and assisted agency under merciful authority
findings.claim: The opening can orient agency toward the worshipped one whose mercy includes aid and whose authority includes judgment.
findings.mechanism: 39:11 makes worship an act directed to Allah; 21:112 combines judgment in truth with seeking help from al-Rahman. The explicit invocation relation in 17:110 joins those designations back to the focus.
findings.reader_payoff: Dependence can coexist with active devotion and accountable authority.
findings.containment: Neither the order of phrases nor this summary proves that yielding must temporally precede or cause aid. Mercy retains beneficence; the authority described remains the object of appeal, not a promise that every requested outcome occurs.

epistemic.reason: The legacy nomination is retained only to the extent independently grounded by the supplied wider Arabic and exact branch facets; its reconstruction is not a staged observation.

findings.title: Naming as sustained orientation
findings.claim: The name invoked can function as a continuing point of directed remembrance with an ethical boundary concerning how names are used.
findings.mechanism: 73:8 joins remembrance of the Lord's name with devotion toward him; 7:180 joins invocation through names with a warning about deviation in them; 43:36 describes turning from remembrance of al-Rahman. These return to ism and al-Rahman as orientation maintained or neglected.
findings.reader_payoff: The naming act can continue to matter after its first utterance.
findings.containment: The image remains directed remembrance, not a literal physical marker, street sign, straight road or guarantee of a traveler's route.

findings.title: Mercy names refer to the same one
findings.claim: The proper name and mercy designations in 1:1 identify one addressee, while the mercy words describe that addressee.
findings.mechanism: 17:110 explicitly places calling Allah and calling al-Rahman as alternative acts directed to the owner of the beautiful names. 2:163 places the full mercy pair after the declaration of one deity; 59:22 repeats the proper name and pair in a single identity declaration.
findings.reader_payoff: The series of names can be heard as one directed invocation with multiple descriptive contributions.
findings.containment: This does not erase differences of meaning between the names or assign the two mercy epithets exclusive classes of recipients. The connection is referential, not a morphological derivation.

epistemic.reason: Independent discovery from the supplied Arabic and exact branch facets. Wider-to-focus return is an inference; these connection records carry no explicit trust labels. Source ranking and reciprocal direction do not establish or defeat the relation.

findings.title: A name does not manufacture its referent's authority
findings.claim: Naming Allah can express allegiance to a definite divine referent; the existence or utterance of a name alone does not create authority.
findings.mechanism: 12:40 puts names given by people and their ancestors beside the absence of authority sent by Allah, then directs worship to him. This acts as a boundary on what the name in the basmala can be claimed to accomplish.
findings.reader_payoff: The invocation's force can be distinguished from a label's supposed power to authorize anything done under it.
findings.containment: The focus does not itself state the polemic of 12:40. The reciprocal note explicitly warns that 1:1 alone does not explain invented names, worship and judgment; the present inference proceeds from those explicit wider statements back to the opening.

epistemic.reason: Independent discovery from the supplied Arabic and exact branch facets. Wider-to-focus return is an inference; these connection records carry no explicit trust labels. Source ranking and reciprocal direction do not establish or defeat the relation.

branch_activations.activation: The difference between naming and authorization limits the operative range of by the name.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Invoking the name identifies orientation without making mere naming a warrant.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus formula is not itself accused of inventing a referent.

findings.title: Designation and the absence of an equal
findings.claim: The name in 1:1 can evoke the distinctness of its referent when heard against the wider challenge concerning any comparable namesake.
findings.mechanism: 19:65 connects sustained worship of the Lord with the question whether any samiyy is known for him. The exact registered naming branch includes both namesake and equality by name or quality; the inquiry returns through ism and Allah.
findings.reader_payoff: The name marks a referent whose status cannot be supplied merely by giving another the same designation.
findings.containment: The source permits namesake and worthy equivalent as coexisting readings. 19:7 uses name and samiyy in human naming; that example limits any inference that ordinary human naming is inherently divine uniqueness. No reading is ranked.

epistemic.reason: Independent discovery from the supplied Arabic and exact branch facets. Wider-to-focus return is an inference; these connection records carry no explicit trust labels. Source ranking and reciprocal direction do not establish or defeat the relation.

findings.title: Naming within embodied use
findings.claim: Invoking Allah's name can place an embodied act of use within an explicit relation to him.
findings.mechanism: 6:118 names Allah's name as mentioned over what is eaten. 2:173 places dedication to other than Allah within a prohibition and describes necessity without sin beside forgiving mercy. The name and mercy words meet an actual act of consumption with limits.
findings.reader_payoff: The formula's orientation can reach an ordinary bodily act, while mercy appears with a bounded allowance under need.
findings.containment: This is an interpretive relation within the supplied texts, not a present-day legal ruling. The basmala alone does not enumerate permissions, prescribe a full ritual formula, or establish unlimited exceptions.

epistemic.reason: Independent discovery from the supplied Arabic and exact branch facets. Wider-to-focus return is an inference; these connection records carry no explicit trust labels. Source ranking and reciprocal direction do not establish or defeat the relation.

findings.title: Mercy as a source of communication
findings.claim: The mercy named in the opening can describe a source that addresses its recipients, through a sending-down, reminder or word of peace.
findings.mechanism: 41:2 names the source of a sending-down with the exact mercy pair; 36:58 presents peace as a saying from a merciful Lord. 26:5 keeps refusal of a reminder from al-Rahman visible.
findings.reader_payoff: The epithets can orient the reader toward mercy communicated in speech as well as enacted in protection.
findings.containment: The precise larger contents of the sending-down and the scene surrounding the saying are not imported. Mercy's communication does not entail that every recipient accepts it.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Invoking these epithets can evoke receiving direction or peace from the merciful source.

findings.title: Mercy as a declared commitment

findings.containment: These statements coexist without ranking or a mechanical general/special equation between al-Rahman and al-Rahim. Punishment also remains explicit in 7:156.

findings.title: Mercy and the possibility of return
findings.claim: Mercy can provide the opening for a person's return as well as accompany the reception of that return.
findings.mechanism: 9:118 explicitly describes divine turning toward people so that they may turn; 2:37 gives received words followed by divine turning, ending in al-Rahim. 6:54 retains the person's repentance and repair.

findings.title: Mercy as grounds for renewed hope
findings.claim: The mercy named in the opening can sustain approach after wrongdoing rather than confine mercy to those who have never failed.
findings.mechanism: 39:53 addresses those who have exceeded against themselves and forbids despair of Allah's mercy, ending with al-Rahim; 6:54 explicitly retains repentance and repair.
findings.reader_payoff: The invocation remains approachable to a person aware of wrongdoing.
findings.containment: The text's breadth of forgiveness and the concrete call to return coexist. This finding promises no individual verdict and removes no accountability.

epistemic.reason: Independent discovery from the supplied Arabic and exact branch facets. Wider-to-focus return is an inference; these connection records carry no explicit trust labels. Source ranking and reciprocal direction do not establish or defeat the relation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
branch_activations.carrier: Mercy includes beneficence to one in need.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Those who have wronged themselves are addressed with a ban on despair of mercy; another text specifies return and repair.
branch_activations.activation: The mercy epithet meets an explicitly compromised recipient rather than an idealized one.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Invoking merciful Allah can be an approach from failure toward renewed hope.
branch_activations.boundary: This is neither acquittal of a particular person nor a permission to continue harm.

findings.title: Refuge in the merciful one
findings.claim: The merciful name can be invoked for refuge from another, while the wider texts retain the impossibility of securing independent protection against the named authority.
findings.mechanism: 19:18 explicitly seeks refuge in al-Rahman from an addressee; 21:42 asks who guards people from al-Rahman, and 67:20 challenges an army's capacity to help independently of him.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening can express dependence upon merciful protection while retaining the authority of its referent.
findings.containment: The refuge statement is an appeal, not a guarantee that its speaker controls the outcome. The opposed prepositional relations are retained: refuge in al-Rahman and protection from him are different claims.

epistemic.reason: Independent discovery from the supplied Arabic and exact branch facets. Wider-to-focus return is an inference; these connection records carry no explicit trust labels. Source ranking and reciprocal direction do not establish or defeat the relation.

branch_activations.carrier: Mercy involves care and protection.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The same designation is the referent of refuge in 19:18 and the limit of independent protection in the two challenges.
branch_activations.activation: Protective appeal and sovereign power converge on the epithet.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Invoking al-Rahman can express vulnerable reliance without turning the name into a controlled protective device.
branch_activations.boundary: The wider warnings remain visible; mercy is not reduced to invulnerability.

findings.title: Mercy need not produce acceptance
findings.claim: Beneficent mercy and the recipient's acceptance are distinguishable; mercy language does not warrant an automatic moral transformation.
findings.mechanism: 23:75 states that even mercy and removal of distress would leave the recipients persisting in transgression. 25:60 depicts refusal at the mention of al-Rahman and a command to prostrate.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening's merciful designation describes the named one without certifying the speaker's or hearer's response.
findings.containment: 23:75 is a conditional counter-reading concerning its stated recipients, not a universal claim that mercy fails. 25:60 records refusal rather than endorsing it. The reciprocal 23:75 note cautions that the formula alone does not clarify its condition; the wider explicit condition supplies this return.

findings.title: The merciful designation of the creator
findings.claim: The mercy named at the opening can characterize the maker of the created setting, extending the reader's attention beyond mercy as relief after suffering.
findings.mechanism: 67:3 explicitly speaks of the creation of al-Rahman and its observable coherence; 25:59 likewise names the creator of heavens and earth as al-Rahman. The return is through that exact epithet, whose registered core includes effective benefit and divine breadth.
findings.reader_payoff: Mercy can be heard in the life-setting's coming to be, alongside its later protective and reparative effects.
findings.containment: The link is an inference from the supplied designation of the creator. It neither explains every event nor infers cosmological particulars absent from the packet.

epistemic.reason: The creator-designation and inspection language are explicit in the supplied Arabic; beneficent-creation resonance is the interpreter's inference. No trust label is supplied on these connection records.
